questions.stem: Before cutting parts from a bar, what should you check against the drawing or cutting list?
options: The colour the parts will be painted later
The sizes, number of pieces and material
The name of the person who will weld them
The weight of the offcut bin by the saw

options: So the saw blade stays cooler during the cut
So the marked line is cut off and lost

questions.stem: Which PPE should always be worn when using an abrasive cut-off saw?

questions.stem: Which way should the teeth point when fitting a hacksaw blade?

Both strokes equally

options: Use an engineer's square against the cut end
Look at it from the other side of the room
Tap it on the bench to hear the sound
Hold it up against the light

questions.stem: What is a burr?
options: A mark made by the scriber on the metal

questions.stem: Which tool is most often used to remove burrs from a sawn edge?
options: A scriber

Use it as it is, as 2 mm is close enough

questions.stem: Which tools are best for marking a line at 90° across a bar before sawing?
options: A long tape measure on its own
A spirit level and a carpenter's pencil
An engineer's square and a scriber
A pair of dividers and nothing else

questions.stem: Why is a fine scribed line better than a thick chalk line for accurate cutting?
options: Chalk makes the saw blade go blunt faster
Chalk is never allowed in a metal workshop

questions.stem: How should sharp offcuts and metal chips be cleared from a machine?
options: With a brush or hook, after the machine stops
With bare hands while the blade is still running
By blowing them away with an air line

questions.stem: How should long lengths of steel bar be carried in the workshop?
options: By one person, balanced on the shoulder at a run
By two people, one at each end
Dragged along the floor by one end
Thrown onto the rack from a distance

options: Leave them on the floor beside the saw
Put them all in the general rubbish bin

options: It makes the saw run too quietly to hear
It uses up less coolant than a sharp one
It cuts slowly, overheats and can wander
It weighs more than a new, sharp blade

options: Stop the machine, keep clear and report it
Reach in and pull the blade out at once

essays.stem: Describe the main hazards of mechanical cutting machines in the workshop, and how guards, PPE and safe habits control them.
essays.modelAnswer: Cutting machines have moving blades and discs that can cut or crush fingers, catch loose clothing or hair, and throw out chips, sparks or pieces of a broken disc. They are also noisy, and cut edges are sharp. Guards keep hands away from blades and catch flying pieces, so they must always be in place and set close to the work; a machine with a missing or broken guard must not be used. PPE protects against what the guard cannot: safety glasses or a face shield against chips and sparks, hearing protection for saws and grinders, safety boots, and gloves when handling sharp sheet, but no loose gloves near a turning blade. Safe habits include tying back hair and removing rings, clamping the work, keeping hands clear, never leaving a running machine, isolating it before changing a blade, and keeping the floor clear.
markingPoints: Names the hazards: cuts, entanglement, flying pieces, noise, sharp edges
Guards always in place and set close; machine with a faulty guard not used
Suitable PPE: eye and face, hearing, boots, gloves for handling sheet only
Safe habits: hair tied back, no rings, work clamped, hands clear
Isolates before changing a blade, and keeps the floor clear

essays.stem: Describe how to choose, fit and use a hacksaw blade to cut a piece of 25 mm square mild steel bar accurately.
essays.modelAnswer: For 25 mm solid mild steel, choose a blade of about 18 or 24 teeth per 25 mm, so that at least three teeth are always touching the work. Fit the blade with the teeth pointing forward, away from the handle, and tighten the wing nut until the blade is firm. Mark the cutting line with a square and scriber, then clamp the bar in the vice with the line close to the jaws. Start the cut on the waste side of the line with a few light strokes, or file a small nick to start the blade. Use slow, steady strokes, about one a second, with the full length of the blade, pressing on the forward stroke and easing off on the return. Keep the saw upright. Ease off as you finish so that the piece does not snap off, then file off the burr and check the cut with a square.
markingPoints: Chooses a blade so that at least three teeth touch the work
Fits the blade with the teeth forward and tensions it
Marks the line and clamps the bar close to the vice jaws
Slow, full-length strokes, pressing forward and easing off on the return
Eases off at the end, removes the burr and checks the cut

essays.stem: Describe how to cut a sheet of 1.2 mm mild steel to size on a guillotine safely.
essays.modelAnswer: Check the capacity plate to make sure that 1.2 mm mild steel is within the machine's limit, and check that the guards and hold-down are in place and working. Wear safety glasses, safety boots and gloves for handling the sheet. Mark the cutting line on the sheet, or set the back stop to the size needed. Make sure no one else is near the blade or the foot pedal. Slide the sheet in from the front, square against the side guide, until the line sits on the cutting edge or the sheet touches the back stop. Keep both hands on the sheet in front of the guard, well clear of the blade and hold-down. Press the pedal firmly in one smooth stroke. Remove the cut piece, deburr the edges if needed, and check the size. Put offcuts in the scrap bin.
markingPoints: Checks the capacity plate, guards and hold-down
Wears safety glasses, boots and gloves for handling sheet
Sets the size by the marked line or the back stop, with no one else at the machine
Keeps hands in front of the guard and cuts in one smooth stroke
Deburrs, checks the size and clears the offcuts

essays.stem: Explain how to choose and use snips to cut a straight line and a curve in thin sheet metal, and how to avoid injury and a poor edge.
essays.modelAnswer: Check that the sheet is thin enough for hand snips, as the maker states. Use straight snips for straight lines and gentle curves, and left-cut or right-cut snips for tighter curves in that direction. Mark the line clearly. For a straight cut, open the snips wide and make long cuts, but do not close the tips right to the end of each cut, as this leaves small steps in the edge. Let the waste curl away from you, and support the sheet so that it does not drop or flap. For a curve, cut away most of the waste first, then follow the line with short cuts, turning the sheet as you go. Wear gloves and safety glasses, because the cut edges and curls of waste are very sharp. File off any burrs and check the shape against the drawing or template.
markingPoints: Checks the sheet is within the snips' capacity and chooses the right snips
Straight cut: snips opened wide, tips not closed at the end of each cut
Curve: waste removed first, then short cuts following the line
Wears gloves and safety glasses against sharp edges
Deburrs and checks the shape against the drawing

essays.stem: Describe the safe use of an abrasive cut-off saw, from checking the disc to finishing the cut.
essays.modelAnswer: First check that the disc is the right type for steel, undamaged, and rated for at least the machine's speed, and that it is fitted correctly with the right flanges. Check that the guard is in place and moves freely. Make sure there is nothing that can burn in the line of the sparks and that no one is standing in that line. Put on eye and face protection, hearing protection and gloves. Clamp the work firmly in the saw's vice so that it cannot move or twist. Stand to one side, out of line with the disc, start the saw and let it reach full speed. Lower the disc onto the work with steady, light pressure and let the disc do the cutting; do not force it or twist it. When the cut is finished, let the disc stop before taking the work out. Treat the cut ends as hot and sharp.
markingPoints: Checks the disc type, condition, speed rating and fitting, and the guard
Clears burnables and people from the line of sparks
Wears eye, face and hearing protection and gloves
Clamps the work, stands to one side and lets the disc reach full speed
Steady pressure with no side load; waits for the disc to stop; ends treated as hot

essays.stem: Describe how to set up and use a horizontal bandsaw or power hacksaw to cut lengths of steel bar.
essays.modelAnswer: Check that the machine is in good order: guards fitted, blade sharp and tensioned, the right blade for the material, coolant topped up and the emergency stop working. Mark the length on the bar or set the length stop. Clamp the bar firmly in the machine vice, square to the blade, and support long bars on a stand at the far end. Set the blade guides close to the work. Choose the right speed and feed for the material and size: slower for hard or large sections. Turn on the coolant, start the machine and lower the blade gently onto the work. Keep hands clear while it cuts, and never reach across the blade. Let the machine stop at the end of the cut before taking the piece out. Check the length and squareness, remove the burr, and clear the chips with a brush.
markingPoints: Checks guards, blade, coolant and emergency stop before use
Marks the length or sets the stop; clamps the bar square; supports long bars
Sets the guides close and chooses a suitable speed for the material
Lowers the blade gently and keeps hands clear while it cuts
Waits for the stop, checks the piece, deburrs and clears chips with a brush

essays.stem: Explain how to isolate a cutting machine before changing a blade or clearing a jam, and why this must be done.
essays.modelAnswer: Switch the machine off at its own switch and wait for the blade or disc to stop completely. Then switch off at the isolator, or unplug it if it is a plug-in tool, so that no power can reach it. Fit your own padlock to the isolator and a tag with your name and the reason, so that no one else can switch it on while you work. Press the start button to prove that the machine will not start, then return the switch to off. Only then change the blade or clear the jam, using gloves and the right tools. When the work is finished, refit all the guards, remove your lock and tag, and test the machine. This must be done because someone who does not know you are working on it could start the machine, and a moving blade can cause serious injury.
markingPoints: Switches off and waits for the blade to stop
Switches off at the isolator or unplugs the tool
Fits a personal lock and a tag
Proves the machine will not start before working on it
Refits guards before restoring power, and explains why isolation is needed

essays.stem: Explain how to plan cutting from a cutting list so that waste is kept low. Include the allowance for the saw cut and how to mark out.
essays.modelAnswer: First read the cutting list and the drawing, and check the sizes, number of pieces and material needed. Check the lengths of stock bar or sheet in the store. Plan which pieces will come from each length so that the offcuts are as small as possible: cut the longest pieces first and fit short pieces into what is left. Allow for the width of each saw cut (the kerf), usually 1–3 mm depending on the saw, and for trimming any rough or out-of-square ends. Write the plan down or sketch it. Mark out from one end of the bar, measuring each piece from a squared end, using a square and scriber. Mark the waste side of each line with a cross so that the cut is made in the right place. Label the pieces as they are cut.
markingPoints: Reads the cutting list and drawing and checks the stock
Plans the longest pieces first and fits short pieces into what is left
Allows for the kerf and for trimming the ends
Marks out from a squared end with a square and scriber
Marks the waste side of each line and labels the pieces

essays.stem: Describe how to check cut parts for size, squareness and finish, and what to do with a part that is outside the tolerance.
essays.modelAnswer: After cutting, remove the burrs with a file so that measurements are true and the parts are safe to handle. Measure each length with a steel rule or tape from the squared end and compare it with the drawing and its tolerance, for example ±1 mm. Check squareness by holding an engineer's square against the side and the cut end and looking for light between them. Check that the cut edge is straight and clean, with no deep saw marks or heat damage. Count the pieces against the cutting list and label them. If a part is too long, trim it and measure again. If it is too short or badly out of square, do not use it: set it aside, mark it as rejected and tell the instructor, so that a new piece can be cut and the cause can be found.
markingPoints: Deburrs before measuring
Measures each part and compares it with the drawing and tolerance
Checks squareness with an engineer's square
Checks the finish of the cut edge, counts and labels the parts
Trims parts that are long; sets aside and reports parts that are short or out of square

essays.stem: Describe how to clean up and look after cutting tools and machines at the end of a job, and how to report faults.
essays.modelAnswer: Switch off and isolate machines before cleaning them, and wait for blades to stop. Use a brush, not your hands or an air line, to clear chips from saws, guillotines and benches. Wipe the machines down and put a light coat of oil on bare surfaces if the maker says to. Release the tension on bandsaw or hacksaw blades if that is the Centre's rule. Check blades and discs for wear or damage, and change or report them. Clean hand tools such as snips, hacksaws, files, squares and tapes, and put them away in their proper places. Sort the offcuts: useful pieces to the rack and scrap to the scrap bin. Sweep the floor. Report any fault, such as a damaged guard, a blunt or cracked blade, or a machine that sounds wrong, to the instructor, and tag the machine out of use until it is repaired.
markingPoints: Switches off, isolates and waits for blades to stop before cleaning
Clears chips with a brush, not hands or an air line
Looks after the machines: wipes and oils, blade tension, checks blades and discs
Puts hand tools away, sorts offcuts and sweeps the floor
Reports faults to the instructor and tags the machine out of use

practical1.title: Cutting steel sections to a cutting list with hand and power saws
practical1.brief: As a group, cut a set of parts for a small steel frame from a cutting list: lengths of 25 mm × 25 mm × 3 mm angle and 25 mm square tube, some with a 45° mitre at one end. Plan the cuts together to keep waste low. Each member marks out and cuts at least two pieces by hand with a hacksaw, and at least two on the bandsaw or power hacksaw (or on the abrasive cut-off saw, if the Centre's rules allow it), while the assessor watches. Each member deburrs and checks their own pieces for length and squareness, and the group lays all the parts out and labels them against the cutting list. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the parts are checked and the area is clean.
materials: 25 mm × 25 mm × 3 mm mild steel angle and 25 mm square tube, in stock lengths
Cutting list and drawing for the frame
Hacksaws with 18 and 24 teeth per 25 mm blades
Horizontal bandsaw or power hacksaw (abrasive cut-off saw if allowed)
Steel rule, tape measure, engineer's square, mitre square or protractor, and scriber
Bench vices, files and marking blue
photos: The cutting plan written out, with the stock lengths
Pieces marked out, with the waste side of each line crossed
A member sawing by hand, with the work clamped close to the vice jaws
The power saw set up with the guard on, guides close and the bar clamped
Cut pieces deburred, with a square on a cut end
All the parts laid out and labelled against the cutting list
The saws and benches cleaned, and the offcuts sorted
checklist: Wore safety glasses and boots, and hearing protection at the power saw; hair and loose clothing secured
Marked out accurately from a squared end, with the waste side marked
Fitted and tensioned a suitable hacksaw blade, and sawed with steady, full-length strokes
Set up the power saw safely: guard on, guides close, work clamped, hands clear
Own pieces within ±1 mm of the cutting list and square at the ends (mitres at 45°)
Removed all burrs and labelled own pieces
Cleaned up with a brush, sorted offcuts and left the machines safe
safety: Never use a saw with a guard missing or damaged; tag it and tell the instructor
Isolate the power saw before changing or adjusting the blade
Clamp all work; keep hands well clear and never reach across a moving blade
Clear chips with a brush, never with bare hands or an air line
Wear gloves to handle sharp offcuts, but keep loose gloves away from moving blades

practical2.title: Cutting sheet metal blanks for a small tray with a guillotine and snips
practical2.brief: As a group, cut the sheet blanks for small open trays from 0.9 mm or 1.2 mm mild steel or galvanised sheet. Each member cuts one rectangular blank, about 250 mm × 200 mm, on the guillotine while the assessor watches, then marks and cuts the four corner notches with snips, and cuts one curved shape (a rounded corner or a circle of about 100 mm) with curved-cut snips. Each member checks their blank against the drawing with a rule and square and files off the burrs, and the group lays all the blanks out for checking. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the blanks are checked and the area is clean.
materials: 0.9 mm or 1.2 mm mild steel or galvanised sheet, within the guillotine's rated capacity
Drawing of the tray blank with its sizes and corner notches
Guillotine with its guards and hold-down
Steel rule, engineer's square, scriber, dividers and marking blue
Files, and gloves for handling sheet
photos: The guillotine checked: capacity plate, guard and hold-down
A sheet being fed square against the side guide, with hands behind the guard
A cut blank marked out for its corner notches
A curved shape cut with curved-cut snips
All the blanks deburred and laid out, with a square on one corner
The area cleaned, with sharp offcuts in the scrap bin
checklist: Wore safety glasses, boots and gloves for handling the sheet
Checked the capacity plate and guards before using the guillotine
Kept hands behind the guard and worked the pedal alone, in one smooth stroke
Marked out the notches and curve accurately from the drawing
Chose the right snips and cut cleanly to the line, without steps or tears
Own blank within ±1 mm of the drawing, square at the corners and deburred
Cleared offcuts safely and left the guillotine and bench tidy
safety: Only one person at the guillotine at a time; nobody else near the blade or pedal
Never cut sheet thicker or harder than the guillotine's rated capacity
Wear gloves and safety glasses: cut edges and curls of waste are very sharp
Put offcuts straight into the scrap bin; never leave them on the floor
Report any fault with the guillotine at once and tag it out of use
